segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — May 14, 2019:

Mr. Bunker commented he was pleased with the High School’s accomplishments. He said he was also proud of the Recreation Department. He reported this week was police week and there was an open house at the Police Department on the 15th from 5-7:30. He said they had an outstanding department. He reported the Memorial Day Breakfast would be hosted by the Fire Department.

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: Swearing in of four police officers

segments.text: Mayor Frost reported he was grateful to work with great people who are making American Fork great. He said the staff and Council were great people. He stated that he was pleased about the swearing in of four new officers to the American Fork Police Department. He paid tribute to Chief Falslev. He stated that 3 of the 4 recruits were attracted to American Fork because they wanted to work with Chief Falslev.

Council Member Carroll explained this included one additional item sent out. She shared a story about an accident that occurred a few days ago involving one of the police officers where the officer was at a stop sign when a car turned the corner and hit the patrol car head on. Luckily no one was seriously injured.

Council Member Taylor commented the protection of the quality of life was the Council’s job. He noted there was not enough money to hire enough enforcement officers. He said he agreed with what had been discussed and thought they needed to rewrite the ordinance. They needed better enforcement and restrictions before they passed the ordinance.

Council member Taylor said they needed to decide where they permitted short-term rentals. Council Member Shelton and Christensen agreed.

Council Member Barnes commented he wanted to support personal property rights. He noted this issue affected people’s property rights and neighbors. He said they needed to investigate how this would affect the residents and the police force. He noted he had been called by residents that had issues. He said the police needed to be contacted when there were problems. He said they needed to create an ordinance to get experience.
